root_cause.text: btrfs reflink of inline extents could dirty a destination folio beyond the inode’s current i_size without updating i_size first, so later flushoncommit writeback tried to invalidate that folio while the reflink still held the extent io-tree lock and was itself blocked on starting a new transaction, creating a circular wait.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (ret == 0 && new_key->offset + datal > i_size_read(&inode->vfs_inode)) i_size_write(&inode->vfs_inode, new_key->offset + datal);` in `clone_copy_inline_extent()` and explicitly states this is needed “before we start a transaction to update the inode item” to prevent the deadlock when `copy_inline_to_page()` places data beyond EOF and `btrfs_invalidate_folio()` later blocks on `btrfs_lock_extent_bits()` under `flushoncommit`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Advance the destination inode size before starting a transaction when cloning inline extents past EOF to prevent a flush-on-commit deadlock.
intent_record.what: After copying inline extent data into a page/folio, the code now checks whether the end of the copied range extends past the destination inode's current i_size, and if so calls i_size_write() to grow i_size before jumping to the existing out path. The change adds a large explanatory comment describing the deadlock scenario that motivates this early i_size update.
intent_record.how: This makes the destination inode appear larger immediately after the inline data is copied, before a transaction is started to update the inode item. As a result, later delalloc writeback will not treat the newly dirtied folio as beyond EOF and try to invalidate it while reflink code still holds extent locks, avoiding the described deadlock during flush-on-commit operation.

grouping_result.intent: Advance the destination inode size before starting a transaction when cloning inline extents past EOF to prevent a flush-on-commit deadlock.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it advances the destination inode size before transaction start when cloning inline extents past EOF, which prevents writeback from dirtying/invalidation against an undersized i_size and avoids the flush-on-commit deadlock described.

candidates.rationale: This statement performs the inline extent clone into the destination page/folio before any size advancement is visible, which is the operation that can dirty data beyond the inode's current i_size and trigger the later flushoncommit deadlock.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the inline extent clone operation that dirties the destination folio before the inode size is advanced or a transaction is started, matching the root cause that led to flush-on-commit writeback deadlock.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function is `clone_copy_inline_extent()` and it already contains the key mitigation for the reported reflink/flushoncommit deadlock scenario: when the destination inline extent is copied into page cache, the code updates the inode state and range tracking. In particular, after dropping/creating the extent it calls `btrfs_update_inode_bytes(inode, datal, drop_args.bytes_found);`, `btrfs_set_inode_full_sync(inode);`, and `btrfs_inode_set_file_extent_range(inode, 0, aligned_end);`. The change from `i_size_read(dst)` to `i_size_read(&inode->vfs_inode)` is only the internal-interface refactor and does not show the buggy behavior. The vulnerable construct described in the root cause — dirtying a destination folio beyond i_size without first updating i_size, leading to a circular wait with writeback and transaction start — is not present in this snippet. Since the code shown already has the inline-extent handling path that updates inode bookkeeping, this function body does not exhibit the vulnerability.
